intro: Regarding the translation of Hegel’s Greater Logic, readers have kindly alerted me to a number of errors. Most are innocuous, but two are serious. I have documented all in three notes published in the Owl of Minerva.

items.title: Corrections Regarding the Recent Translation of Hegel’s ‘Greater Logic’
items.summary: The first list of errors, two of them serious: at p. 386, ‘pure reflection’ should read ‘pure negativity’; at p. 723, a subordinate clause is attached to the wrong line.

items.title: A Second Note Regarding the Recent Translation of Hegel’s ‘Greater Logic’
items.summary: Two typographical errors in Remark 1 on the calculus (pp. 235 and 241) that entered Hegel’s own text in the 1832 edition and have been reproduced without comment in every subsequent edition and English translation since.

items.title: One More Note on the Translation of Hegel’s Science of Logic
items.summary: An error at p. 705 in Hegel’s illustration from Gauss, with the history of the 1923 Lasson emendation that stood behind it; a correction at p. 74; and four further corrections provided by readers.
